findings.location: Section 'Schedule changes', wizard-steps block (div.wizard-steps, ids s3-step1 to s3-step3)
findings.evidence: <div class="step" id="s3-step3" style="order:3"> 'Confirm your order' appears first in the DOM, <div class="step" id="s3-step2" style="order:2"> 'Enter payment details' second, <div class="step" id="s3-step1" style="order:1"> 'Choose a plan' third.
findings.violation: The three step divs' DOM order (Confirm your order, then Enter payment details, then Choose a plan) is the reverse of the order their declared CSS order values impose (order:1 Choose a plan first, order:2 Enter payment details second, order:3 Confirm your order third), so a reader encountering the content linearized hears the confirm-and-pay step before the step establishing what is being chosen.
findings.fix: Reorder the three step divs in the DOM to match the intended reading sequence (Choose a plan, Enter payment details, Confirm your order) instead of relying on the CSS order property to reorder them only visually.

findings.location: Section 'Schedule changes', div.icon-delete (id s3-customcontrol), the custom control after the 'Refresh status' button
findings.violation: The custom-built delete control, a div styled and named as an icon-only delete action, carries no role, no accessible name (its only content is an img explicitly marked decorative with alt=""), and no tabindex making it keyboard-reachable, so assistive technology cannot detect that the control exists, name it, or reach it by keyboard.
findings.fix: Rebuild the control as a native <button> with a visible or aria-label of 'Delete', or add role="button", an accessible name, tabindex="0", and a keydown handler to the existing div.

findings.location: Section 'Schedule changes', form field label 'Phone number' (id s3-form-phone-label)
findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>, compared against sibling labels 'Route', 'Email address', and 'Promo code', none of which carry a color declaration.
findings.violation: The 'Phone number' label is distinguished from its three sibling labels only by red text color (#cc0000), with no asterisk, 'required' text, icon, or other non-color signal explaining what the color denotes.
findings.fix: Add a text or icon signal alongside the color, for example an asterisk plus a note explaining what red denotes, or remove the color if it carries no meaning, so the distinction survives without color.

findings.location: Header navigation (nav id="nav"), the page's only navigation mechanism
findings.evidence:
Plan a tripService alerts
is the only navigation mechanism in the document; no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere, and the footer holds only a privacy link and a terms link.
findings.violation: The page exposes exactly one of the five navigation mechanisms, a primary navigation menu, with no site search, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail present anywhere in the markup, and nothing in the page marks it as one step in a linear process.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent way to reach this page, such as a site search form or a breadcrumb trail, rather than relying on the primary navigation menu alone.

findings.location: Section 'Schedule changes', form, promo code field error text (id s3-form-promo-error)
findings.evidence: Error., with no aria-describedby on the input pointing at the span.
findings.violation: The promo-code field's error text reads only 'Error.', naming neither the field nor what is wrong with the value entered, and the span is not linked to the input through aria-describedby, so a screen reader does not necessarily announce it when the field receives focus.
findings.fix: Replace 'Error.' with text naming the field and the specific problem, for example 'Promo code not recognized, check for typos', and associate it to the input with aria-describedby.
